questions.question_text:
A removalist truck driver has a tax payable of $\$16\,940$ and his PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$18\,315$.
What is his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Ignored the instalments already withheld and treated the whole tax payable as still owing.
Added the two totals together instead of subtracting to find the balance.
Gave the total instalments rather than the amount by which they exceed the tax payable.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total instalments}-\text{Total tax payable}=18\,315-16\,940$
$=1375$
The balance is positive, so he receives a tax refund of $\$1375.00$.

questions.question_text:
A grain-harvest worker has a tax payable of $\$7825$ and his PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$8190$.
Which statement correctly describes his year-end tax position?

options.text: A refund, because his instalments are greater than his tax payable
An amount owing, because his tax payable is greater than his instalments
options.why: Compared the two totals the wrong way round: $\$8190$ is the larger amount, not $\$7825$.

options.text: A refund, because his tax payable is greater than his instalments
options.why: Reached the right outcome with the wrong reasoning; too much tax withheld, not too little, produces a refund.

options.text: An amount owing, because his instalments are greater than his tax payable
options.why: Treated instalments above the tax payable as a shortfall rather than as an overpayment.

questions.solution_text:
Compare the two totals.
$8190>7825$
More tax was withheld than was actually payable, so he receives a refund.

questions.question_text:
A poultry-farm worker has a tax payable of $\$10\,296$ and her PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$10\,296$.
What is her tax refund or amount owing?

options.text: Neither a refund nor an amount owing

options.why: Treated the whole of the instalments withheld as a refund because nothing further was owing.
Added the tax payable to the instalments instead of subtracting them.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total instalments}-\text{Total tax payable}=10\,296-10\,296$
$=0$
The balance is zero, so there is neither a refund nor an amount owing.

questions.question_text:
A food-delivery courier had $\$276.50$ withheld from each of her $52$ weekly pays.
Her tax payable is $\$14\,120$.
What is her tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Multiplied the weekly instalment by $26$ fortnights instead of by $52$ weeks.
Compared a single week’s instalment with the whole year’s tax payable.
Gave the year’s total instalments rather than the amount left over after the tax payable.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=276.50\times52$
$=\$14\,378$
2. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$14\,378-14\,120=258$
The balance is positive, so she receives a tax refund of $\$258.00$.

questions.question_text:
A livestock transport driver has an income tax payable of $\$11\,594$ and a Medicare levy of $\$1338$.
His PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$12\,470$.
What is his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Compared the instalments with the income tax only, leaving the Medicare levy out of the total tax payable.
Subtracted the Medicare levy from the income tax instead of adding it to find the total tax payable.
Counted the Medicare levy twice, once inside the total tax payable and once again in the balance.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the total tax payable**
$\text{Total tax payable}=11\,594+1338$
$=\$12\,932$
2. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$12\,470-12\,932=-462$
The balance is negative, so he has an amount owing of $\$462.00$.

questions.question_text:
A seasonal cotton-gin worker has a tax payable of $\$13\,482$ and his PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$14\,615$.
What is his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Reversed the subtraction and treated the overpayment as an amount owing.
Added the instalments and tax payable instead of subtracting.
Gave all the instalments paid rather than only the amount above the tax payable.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Total instalments}-\text{Total tax payable}=14\,615-13\,482$
$=1133$
The balance is positive, so he receives a tax refund of $\$1133.00$.

questions.question_text:
A furniture removalist had $\$364.75$ withheld from each of his $26$ fortnightly pays.
His tax payable is $\$10\,186.90$.
What is his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Treated instalments below the tax payable as an overpayment instead of a shortfall.
Multiplied the fortnightly instalment by $12$ months instead of $26$ fortnights.
Subtracted only one fortnight’s instalment from the annual tax payable.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=364.75\times26$
$=\$9483.50$
2. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$9483.50-10\,186.90=-703.40$
The balance is negative, so he has an amount owing of $\$703.40$.

questions.question_text:
A courier van driver has an income tax payable of $\$10\,842$ and a Medicare levy of $\$1264$.
His PAYG instalments for the year totalled $\$11\,350$.
What is his tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Left out the Medicare levy and compared the instalments with income tax only.
Subtracted the Medicare levy from income tax instead of adding it.
Added the Medicare levy twice when finding total tax payable.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the total tax payable**
$\text{Total tax payable}=10\,842+1264$
$=\$12\,106$
2. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$11\,350-12\,106=-756$
The balance is negative, so he has an amount owing of $\$756.00$.

questions.question_text:
A farm supervisor has a taxable income of $\$52\,800$ and had $\$260$ withheld from each of her $26$ fortnightly pays.
$\begin{array}{l|l} \textbf{Taxable income} & \textbf{Tax on this income} \\ \hline \$0\text{ to }\$18\,200 & \text{Nil} \\ \$18\,201\text{ to }\$45\,000 & 19\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$18\,200 \\ \$45\,001\text{ to }\$120\,000 & \$5092\text{ plus }32.5\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$45\,000 \\ \$120\,001\text{ to }\$180\,000 & \$29\,467\text{ plus }37\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$120\,000 \\ \$180\,001\text{ and over} & \$51\,667\text{ plus }45\text{c for each }\$1\text{ over }\$180\,000 \end{array}$
Using the tax table and ignoring the Medicare levy, what is her tax refund or amount owing, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Taxed the whole income at $32.5$c instead of only the excess over $\$45\,000$.
Left out the base tax of $\$5092$ and used only the tax on the excess.
Multiplied the fortnightly instalment by $12$ months instead of by $26$ fortnights.

questions.solution_text:
1. **Find the total tax payable**
$\text{Total tax payable}=5092+0.325\times(52\,800-45\,000)$
$=5092+0.325\times7800$
$=\$7627$
2. **Find the total instalments paid**
$\text{Total instalments}=260\times26$
$=\$6760$
3. **Subtract the total tax payable from the total instalments**
$6760-7627=-867$
The balance is negative, so she has an amount owing of $\$867.00$.
